screens.title: Why do we need tangents?
lines: Look at a cycle wheel on the road. The wheel is round. The road is straight.
Press Roll the wheel and watch where they meet.

ask.q: How many points of the road touch the wheel at one time?
ask.a: Exactly one point. A straight line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent.

screens.title: See it: the stone and the sling
lines: A boy swings a stone in a sling (கவண்). The string is like the radius.
Press Let go. Watch which way the stone flies.

ask.q: When he lets go, does the stone fly away from the centre, or along the edge of the circle?
ask.a: Along the edge, in a straight line. It flies along the tangent, at 90° to the string.

screens.title: Touch it: move the line
lines: Drag the blue line up and down, or use the slider.
Count how many points the line shares with the circle.

ask.q: When does the line touch the circle at exactly one point?
ask.a: When its distance from the centre is exactly equal to the radius. That line is the tangent.

screens.title: Draw it: tangent and radius
lines: Here is a tangent at point P, and the radius OP.
Drag P anywhere around the circle. Watch the angle at P.

ask.q: Move P to five different places. What is the angle between OP and the tangent each time?
ask.a: Always 90°. The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

screens.title: Draw it: tangents from a point
lines: Drag point P inside, onto, and outside the circle.
Count the tangents. When P is outside, compare PA and PB.

ask.q: P is outside the circle. What do you notice about PA and PB?
ask.a: PA = PB always. The two tangents drawn from an outside point are equal in length.

screens.title: The formula, from the picture
lines: OT is the radius. PT is the tangent. The angle at T is 90°, so OTP is a right triangle.
So we can use Pythagoras. Press Next step to build the formula.
card: A tangent touches a circle at **one point**.
Tangent ⊥ radius at the point of contact: **90°**.
From an outside point: **2 tangents**, and **PA = PB**.

ask.q: Radius OT = 6 cm and OP = 10 cm. Find the tangent length PT.

screens.title: Where will I use this?
lines: The straight parts of this chain are tangents to both wheels. Engineers use tangent length to cut the right size of belt or chain.
uses: The straight parts are tangents. Belt length is worked out using tangent length.
When released, the object flies off along the tangent.
A straight road joins a curved road along the tangent, so vehicles don't jerk.
The road is a tangent to the tyre: one point of contact at every moment.
The slope of a tangent is the start of calculus (derivatives). Tangents to circles come again in coordinate geometry.

ask.q: Why must the straight part of a cycle chain be a tangent to the wheel?
ask.a: So the chain leaves the wheel at 90° to the radius, smoothly, with no jerk. Any other angle would make it rub or slip.

screens.title: Say it instantly
lines: First say the five facts together, aloud. Then answer the quick questions on the board.
chant: A tangent touches the circle at one point.
From an outside point: two tangents, PA = PB.

board.intro: Say the five facts together first
board.outro: Well done! Say the five facts once more.
